text:
maria: Heads-up — after regenerating poetry.lock for the tokenizers/transformers CVE patch, CI started failing on FastAPI imports in several services. Error points at starlette dependency mismatches.

maria: (sorry double-post, thread continues below)
kevin: Can you paste the failing log? Is it an import error at runtime or an installation wheel issue?
ada: I saw similar locally — tokenizers wheel fallback to pure-Python variant changed the dependency constraints, which pulled in starlette 0.x vs 1.x mismatch for some internal packages.
rachel: Posting the CI error from the infra job: 
```
ERROR: Exception in ASGI application
ImportError: cannot import name 'URL' from 'starlette.types' (/venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/starlette/types.py)
During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tokenizers._tokenizers'
```
kevin: That ModuleNotFoundError usually means the manylinux wheel wasn't picked up and pip fell back to a sdist. Which means binary wheel incompatibility on the runner.
ci-bot: build 4821 failed on ubuntu-20.04-py3.10 (pip wheel lookup fallback)
security-bot: Note: this lock regen was driven by CVE-2025-2987 tokenizers advisory; patch was to bump tokenizers to 0.13.4+ which included wheel rebuilds.
maria: Okay — two separate problems: (1) wheel/platform mismatch causing tokenizers to fall back to sdist -> runtime import error, (2) transitive starlette upgrade pulled by some internal dependency now failing imports.
ada: Proposed triage plan:
- reproduce locally with same ubuntu image (docker: ubuntu:20.04, python:3.10)
- try `pip install --prefer-binary -r reqs.txt` to see if wheel fixes it
- if wheel unavailable, pin tokenizers to prior safe wheel or add pip constraint to point to a built wheel artifact from CI
- for starlette, identify which package is pulling newer starlette and open constrained backport PR in affected services
kevin: I'll repro the wheel issue in a matrix job. If it's an infra runner config (musl vs glibc or manylinux2014 vs 2010), we should publish a built wheel to our internal artifacts and point prod constraints at it.
rachel: For the starlette import, the failing import path suggests we got starlette 0.27 vs expected 0.30 API. The immediate mitigation is to pin starlette==0.30.1 in the service's constraints and run full integration tests.
maria: Timeline ask: can we get a mitigation PR (pin constraints + pip constraint file referencing internal wheel) in the next 3 hours? We want to keep deploys green for the Dedicated infra run.
kevin: I'll open two PRs: 1) infra/constraints: add tokenizers wheel artifact URL + pin; 2) service-template: pin starlette.
ada: Assigning reviewers: @kevin for the infra PR, @ada for the service template PR, and I'll run the local matrix tests and deploy a canary to staging.
ada: Local repro command I'm using: 
```bash
docker run --rm -it ubuntu:20.04 bash -c "apt update && apt install -y python3.10 python3.10-venv build-essential && python3.10 -m venv /venv && /venv/bin/pip install -U pip wheel setuptools && /venv/bin/pip install -r /workspace/requirements.txt"
```
maria: Also important: we should check whether this change needs a backport to 2024-LTS branch (we still run some clusters on that). If so, follow standard emergency backport flow and include a short changelog mentioning the CVE and wheel pin.
kevin: CI repro done — same failures. Looks like our ubuntu runners are using manylinux2010-compatible glibc so recent tokenizers wheels are built with manylinux2014 and pip isn't picking them up due to platform tags. I'll push a rebuilt wheel to artifacts and update pip constraints.
ci-bot: artifacts: tokenizers-0.13.4-xxx.whl uploaded to s3://redwood-ci-wheels/tokenizers/0.13.4/
rachel: After pinning starlette and pointing to the internal wheel, integration tests pass locally. Need CI matrix run to confirm python 3.9/3.10/3.11.
ada: If CI green, deploy plan: canary to staging (10% traffic) -> monitor error rates for 30m -> promote. If canary fails, automatic rollback via deploy bot.
maria: Security note: add a short audit log entry referencing CVE-2025-2987, wheel pin, and the PR numbers. We'll need that for compliance review later.
kevin: Created PRs: infra#1223 (wheel artifact + pip constraints), service-template#789 (starlette pin). Linking to tokenizers CVE ticket SEC-412.
ada: Running CI now. ETA ~25m.
security-bot: Marking SEC-412 as in-progress; remind to run SBOM regen and update the compliance checklist once PRs merge.
maria: Thanks all — keep updates in this thread. If you hit blockers ping me and I'll escalate to platform infra. :thumbsup:
